question: What does a 'just culture' mean for patient safety in a hospital?

options.A: A strict legal system where every single mistake results in immediate court prosecution
options.B: An administrative rule that hides medical errors from patients and their families
options.C: A policy that protects senior doctors from ever facing disciplinary action
options.D: A work environment where staff can report errors openly to fix system flaws without unfair punishment

explanation: In a just culture, nurses feel safe speaking up about mistakes without fear, helping the whole team learn and protect patients better. [learn more](GST321_U1_T2#GST321_U1_T2_h8)

question: Why is it so helpful for nurses to involve family caregivers in the care plan for an autistic patient?

options.A: Caregivers know the patient's unique routines and communication cues best
options.B: Caregivers have formal medical degrees in nursing care
options.C: Hospital policy legally requires family members to do the nursing work
options.D: It removes all responsibility from the hospital staff

explanation: Family members are absolute experts on their loved one's specific triggers and favorite comforts. Partnering with them makes all the difference! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T5#GNS324_U4_T5_h6)

question: What is a major reason for high maternal mortality rates in many rural Nigerian communities?

options.A: Limited access to skilled birth attendants and emergency obstetric care
options.B: Universal free access to advanced reproductive technology
options.C: Mandatory hospital deliveries for all pregnant women
options.D: An overabundance of licensed gynecologists in primary health centers

explanation: When clinics are far away and transport is hard to find, delays in getting emergency care during childbirth sadly put many mothers at high risk. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T1#GNS216_U1_T1_h4)

question: A new mother who just had a tear repaired with stitches (episiotomy) says she is soaking her private area in very hot water daily for pain. What is the major risk here?

options.A: Instantaneous regeneration of damaged muscle fibers
options.B: Complete prevention of postpartum hemorrhage
options.C: Immediate closure of the surgical wound within minutes
options.D: Tissue maceration and delayed wound healing leading to infection

explanation: Fresh stitches need time to stay clean and dry. Soaking them in hot water makes the skin soggy (macerated), which slows down healing and lets germs in. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T15#GNS312_U1_T15_h3)

question: What breathing instruction do you give a patient right as the doctor is pulling out their chest tube?

options.A: Take a deep breath, hold it, and bear down
options.B: Take rapid, shallow breaths through your mouth
options.C: Cough hard multiple times in quick succession
options.D: Breathe out completely and hold your breath

explanation: Spot on! Doing the Valsalva maneuver (holding breath and bearing down) boosts pressure in the chest, keeping the lung safely expanded as the tube comes out. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T18#GNS221_U2_T18_h7)

question: What turns a natural hazard like a flood into a disaster?

options.A: When international media reports on it
options.B: When it overwhelms local response capacity
options.C: When it occurs only in rural communities
options.D: When rainfall exceeds historical averages

explanation: A hazard only becomes a disaster when the affected community lacks the resources to handle the scale of destruction on its own. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T11#GNS315_U1_T11_h1)

question: What does follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) do in the ovaries?

options.A: It helps immature eggs inside the ovaries grow.
options.B: It causes the muscular wall of the uterus to contract strongly.
options.C: It immediately stops all blood flow to the endometrium.
options.D: It thickens the outer layer of the vaginal walls.

explanation: True to its name, FSH 'stimulates' the little follicles in the ovary so the eggs inside can grow and get ready for action. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T5#GNS121_U5_T5_h2)

question: How does a positive feedback loop work in the body?

options.A: It stops hormone production the moment a target organ is reached
options.B: It constantly brings a fluctuating variable back to an exact baseline
options.C: It uses neural impulses exclusively to monitor blood calcium levels
options.D: It amplifies or intensifies a physiological change until an event finishes

explanation: Unlike negative feedback, positive feedback pushes a process harder and faster until a specific big event is done—like childbirth! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T6#GNS211_U1_T6_h6)

question: Why is the bedside nurse considered the central link in the healthcare nutrition team?

options.A: They have legal power to prescribe diets
options.B: They do all formal nutrition assessments alone
options.C: They observe daily intake and update the team
options.D: They are the only ones allowed to serve food

explanation: You got it! Because we are always at the bedside, we notice what the patient eats and share that info with the doctors and dietitians. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T001#GNS227_U3_T001_h3)

question: Which tool is most frequently used to gather opinions from large groups in descriptive research?

options.A: Laboratory blood cultures
options.B: Surgical biopsy procedures
options.C: Surveys and questionnaires
options.D: Randomized drug trials

explanation: When you need to hear from many people quickly, questionnaires and surveys are the easiest and most practical tools to use. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h4)

question: Why do researchers clean their data before running statistics?

options.A: To reduce the number of participants needed for the study
options.B: To catch entry mistakes and prevent false research results
options.C: To get extra funding from the hospital research committee
options.D: To make the research report shorter and easier to print

explanation: Data cleaning is like double-checking your medication dosage math—it catches errors early so your final results are accurate and safe. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T16#GNS217_U3_T16_h3)

question: A nurse records a patient's daily urine output as 1000 mL, which is exactly double yesterday's output. What scale makes this math possible?

options.A: Ratio scale
options.B: Interval scale
options.C: Ordinal scale
options.D: Nominal scale

explanation: Because urine output has a true zero (0 mL means absolutely no urine), you can safely make direct comparisons like 'twice as much'. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T1#GNS217_U4_T1_h5)

question: A patient in the ER has a fast heart rate, cool sweaty skin, and slow capillary refill. What do these signs tell you?

options.A: They are simply recovering from light exercise
options.B: The brain and heart are getting plenty of oxygen
options.C: Poor blood flow and possible shock
options.D: The nervous system is just overactive

explanation: Spot on! The body pulls blood away from the skin to protect vital organs like the heart and brain when blood volume is low. Classic signs of shock! [learn more](GNS315_U3_T4#GNS315_U3_T4_h4)

question: Which body regulates the professional conduct and practice of nurses in Nigeria?

options.A: National Association of Nigerian Nurses and Midwives
options.B: Nigerian Medical Association
options.C: Federal Ministry of Health
options.D: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: Spot on! The NMCN is the main statutory body that oversees nursing education and practice standards in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T12#GNS321_U2_T12_h1)

question: What crucial checks must a nurse perform right before handing medication to a patient?

options.A: The political affiliation of the patient
options.B: Patient allergies and correct dosage instructions
options.C: The brand of the car the patient drove toanteen
options.D: The personal phone number of the prescribing doctor

explanation: Patient safety is job number one! Always double-check allergies and doses to prevent adverse drug reactions. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T7#GNS215_U3_T7_h5)

question: Why would a nurse need to provide alternative ways for a patient to pass urine or stool?

options.A: The patient is unable to walk to the toilet independently
options.B: The hospital policy requires all bedridden patients to use bedpans
options.C: It reduces the total amount of daily nursing documentation
options.D: It completely prevents any risk of a hospital-acquired infection

explanation: You've got this! We bring in things like bedpans or urinals mainly when a patient is too weak or restricted to safely make it to the bathroom on their own. Simple and practical! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T8#GNS112_U5_T8_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to prevent software-related mistakes on the ward?

options.A: Disabling all confirmation prompts to make data entry go faster
options.B: Using smart defaults that fill in safe, common choices
options.C: Limiting pop-up warnings only to true clinical hazards
options.D: Designing clear visual layouts with readable fonts

explanation: You nailed it! Confirmation prompts act as a vital safety net. Removing them just to type faster invites accidental medication or charting errors. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h6)

question: A patient who has had three mid-trimester miscarriages is found to have a uterine septum. What is the direct link here?

options.A: Severe chronic high blood pressure in the mother
options.B: Complete closure of the external vaginal opening
options.C: Total cessation of all future ovarian hormone production
options.D: Inability of the growing fetus to find enough room, leading to premature delivery or loss

explanation: Spot on! A uterine septum acts like a wall inside the room, leaving less space for the baby as it grows larger during the second trimester. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T19#GNS216_U5_T19_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a good topic for patient education regarding dietary supplements?

options.A: Bringing all supplement containers to clinic appointments for review
options.B: Checking for valid NAFDAC registration numbers on product labels
options.C: How to manufacture herbal capsules at home in your kitchen
options.D: Reporting unusual side effects or symptoms to a healthcare provider

explanation: As nurses, we teach safety, checking labels, and reporting side effects—we definitely don't encourage brewing or making DIY pills at home! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h7)

question: Why is it best to kick off a research interview with a gentle, friendly icebreaker?

options.A: To test if the audio recorder is working properly
options.B: To help build trust and put the participant at ease
options.C: To quickly finish the interview before shift change
options.D: To trick the participant into sharing secrets

explanation: Exactly! Hospital studies can feel intimidating to patients. A warm, easy start helps them relax and feel safe with you. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T24#GNS224_U1_T24_h3)

question: What life-threatening emergency happens when fluid overload backs up all the way into the lungs?

options.A: Pleural mesothelioma
options.B: Chronic bronchial asthma
options.C: Spontaneous pneumothorax
options.D: Acute pulmonary edema

explanation: When the kidneys can't clear fluid, it backs up into the air sacs (alveoli) of the lungs, causing acute pulmonary edema and severe breathing distress. You're mastering critical care concepts! [learn more](GNS213_U4_T4#GNS213_U4_T4_h8)

question: What is usually the very first step public health teams take when investigating a suspected disease outbreak?

options.A: Hold a press conference on national television
options.B: Close down all schools and markets in the entire country
options.C: Burn medical waste to destroy any remaining bacteria
options.D: Verify the diagnosis and confirm that an outbreak actually exists

explanation: Correct! Before launching a full investigation, health workers must make sure laboratory results and case numbers truly point to an outbreak. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T90#GNS214_U1_T90_h6)

question: During which stages of pregnancy do women usually need an extra 340 to 450 calories every day?

options.A: The first two weeks after conception
options.B: First trimester only
options.C: During labor and delivery
options.D: Second and third trimesters

explanation: As that little baby starts growing super fast in the later months, the mother needs a small energy boost of extra daily calories! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T012#GNS227_U2_T012_h2)

question: What goes wrong in hyperproliferative skin conditions like psoriasis?

options.A: Skin cells multiply much faster than normal and pile up on the surface
options.B: Melanocytes completely disappear from the deepest layer of the dermis
options.C: Sebaceous glands shut down, leaving the skin completely dry and scaly
options.D: Skin cells stop growing entirely, causing deep chronic ulcerations

explanation: Well done! In conditions like psoriasis, cells grow way too fast, creating those thick, raised patches on the skin. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T6#GNS213_U5_T6_h2)

question: During a community health screening, what is the most crucial infection control practice?

options.A: Cleaning stethoscope diaphragms and equipment between every client
options.B: Using disposable paper towels for hand drying only once a day
options.C: Wearing sterile surgical gowns for simple blood pressure checks
options.D: Keeping all the windows closed to prevent dust from entering

explanation: Spot on! Wiping down shared tools between patients is a simple habit that stops germs from spreading. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T5#GNS123_U2_T5_h5)

question: Why is it best to start talking about family planning during antenatal care rather than waiting until after the baby is born?

options.A: Postpartum mothers are too tired to understand reproductive health
options.B: Hospitals forbid mothers from discussing birth control after birth
options.C: It is a legal requirement to purchase contraceptives before leaving the hospital
options.D: It gives parents adequate time to make informed choices about birth spacing

explanation: Bringing it up during ANC gives couples plenty of calm time to talk about birth spacing before the rush and exhaustion of newborn care sets in. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h7)

question: Which mineral shortage causes anemia and makes it hard for children to focus and learn?

options.A: Potassium
options.B: Zinc
options.C: Calcium
options.D: Iron

explanation: You got it! Iron helps make hemoglobin to carry oxygen around the body. Without enough of it, kids feel tired and find it tough to concentrate. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T006#GNS227_U2_T006_h3)

question: When is the best time to document patient care and assessments?

options.A: Before performing the actual physical assessment
options.B: Immediately after the care is provided
options.C: Whenever the head nurse requests a chart review
options.D: At the end of the 12-hour shift from memory

explanation: Always chart right away! Waiting until the end of a long, tiring shift makes it easy to forget important details. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T6#GNS113_U2_T6_h4)

question: A cancer patient on a Step Two weak opioid still has severe pain. What should you do next?

options.A: Continue the current dose because ladder steps cannot be skipped
options.B: Discontinue all pain medications until the pain resolves naturally
options.C: Encourage the patient to rely strictly on relaxation breathing
options.D: Advocate for moving up to Step Three with a strong opioid

explanation: The pain ladder is flexible! If a weaker step isn't cutting it, it's time to step up to stronger medications to keep the patient comfortable. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T2#GNS223_U5_T2_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of the pulmonary circulation system?

options.A: To deliver nutrient-rich blood directly to the brain
options.B: To pump blood against a very high vascular resistance
options.C: To filter waste products out of systemic blood vessels
options.D: To exchange carbon dioxide for oxygen in the lungs

explanation: The primary function of pulmonary circulation is to move blood through the lungs so carbon dioxide can be dropped off and fresh oxygen picked up. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h1)

question: A patient asks why they must finish all their antibiotics even after feeling better. What is the best response?

options.A: Stopping early can let stronger, resistant bacteria survive and cause a worse infection
options.B: Pharmacies will not accept returned medication bottles once opened
options.C: The remaining pills are needed to improve your daily sleep cycle
options.D: Unfinished pills will permanently alter your blood type if thrown away

explanation: Spot on! Stopping early leaves the toughest germs alive to breed resistance. Patient education here stops superbugs from spreading! [learn more](GST114_U5_T3#GST114_U5_T3_h8)

question: Why do hospital disaster plans include steps for safely discharging stable patients?

options.A: To free up critical bed space and medical resources for incoming disaster casualties
options.B: To comply with international travel regulations for foreign medical volunteers
options.C: To punish patients who have overstayed their expected recovery duration
options.D: To reduce the hospital's monthly utility bills during a crisis event

explanation: When an emergency brings in dozens of critically injured people, sending home stable patients creates the vital bed space needed to save lives. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T7#GNS315_U1_T7_h6)

question: What does 'unconditional acceptance' mean when practicing non-judgmental nursing?

options.A: Treating the patient as a human in need of help without moralizing
options.B: Allowing family members to perform nursing duties at the bedside
options.C: Waiving all hospital bills for emergency surgical procedures
options.D: Agreeing with every personal life choice the patient has ever made

explanation: It means leaving your personal opinions at the door. Your only job is to care for the sick human being sitting in front of you. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T024#GNS226_U5_T024_h3)

question: Which of these is a late sign that a patient is running low on oxygen in their blood?

options.A: Hypertension
options.B: Cyanosis
options.C: Tachycardia
options.D: Sweating

explanation: Cyanosis—that bluish tint to the lips and skin—shows up when oxygen levels have been dropping for a bit. It's a classic clinical cue to act fast! [learn more](GNS315_U3_T5#GNS315_U3_T5_h2)

question: What is the main job of neurons?

options.A: To form the bony skull protection
options.B: To produce cerebrospinal fluid exclusively
options.C: To provide structural division without signaling
options.D: To transmit nerve impulses

explanation: Neurons are the electrical wiring specialists of the body, sending messages back and forth like tiny messengers. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T2#GNS211_U3_T2_h7)

question: When mistakes happen in the clinic, what is usually the real root cause?

options.A: Flawed system designs interacting with human limits
options.B: Poor physical fitness and lack of sleep
options.C: A lack of basic nursing education among staff
options.D: Intentional negligence by individual healthcare workers

explanation: You're doing great! Remember that most clinical errors happen because the work environment and tools don't properly support natural human limits—not because nurses are careless. [learn more](GST319_U5_T8#GST319_U5_T8_h1)

question: Why does a toddler often need a higher weight-based drug dose than an infant?

options.A: Accelerated metabolic rates and faster clearance
options.B: Increased thickness of the skin layers
options.C: Complete maturation of the blood-brain barrier
options.D: Lower total body water percentage

explanation: Toddlers have super-active metabolic rates that process and clear certain drugs much faster than tiny infants do. Keep learning, you're doing great! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T6#GNS215_U6_T6_h2)

question: What do we call the bright red vaginal discharge seen in the first few days after birth?

options.A: Colostrum
options.B: Lochia alba
options.C: Lochia rubra
options.D: Lochia serosa

explanation: You nailed it! Lochia rubra is that initial red flow ('rubra' sounds like ruby red) made mostly of blood and tissue during the first few days postpartum. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T013#GNS226_U3_T013_h3)

question: Which routine lab test gives us a quick look at electrolytes like sodium and potassium?

options.A: Basic metabolic panel
options.B: Complete blood count
options.C: Liver function panel
options.D: Lipid profile test

explanation: Spot on! A BMP is your go-to lab panel for checking quick electrolyte and kidney numbers on the ward. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T11#GNS121_U2_T11_h6)

question: Which common bacterium causes most uncomplicated urinary tract infections?

options.A: Streptococcus pyogenes
options.B: Enterococcus faecalis
options.C: Escherichia coli
options.D: Pseudomonas aeruginosa

explanation: E. coli lives happily in our bowels, but when it enters the urinary tract, it becomes the number one culprit behind everyday UTIs! [learn more](GNS223_U8_T2#GNS223_U8_T2_h2)

question: Which of these is a common health problem that shows up after a major disaster?

options.A: Psychological trauma and PTSD
options.B: Increased availability of specialized surgeons
options.C: Immediate financial surplus
options.D: Enhanced community infrastructure

explanation: Great job! Survivors often deal with deep emotional distress and mental health challenges long after their physical wounds heal. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T12#GNS315_U1_T12_h3)

question: What does a spiritual assessment in palliative care mostly focus on?

options.A: Memorization of sacred religious texts
options.B: Meaning, purpose, and inner peace
options.C: Regular attendance at local religious services
options.D: Donations made to charitable organizations

explanation: Spirituality isn't just about religion—it's about helping a patient find hope, peace, and meaning in their journey. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T4#GNS321_U4_T4_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of pre-positioned warehouses set up around the world by disaster agencies?

options.A: To collect financial taxes from incoming humanitarian workers
options.B: To store emergency supplies strategically around the globe for rapid dispatch
options.C: To manufacture local pharmaceutical drugs during an epidemic
options.D: To serve as permanent housing units for refugees fleeing conflict

explanation: You got it! Keeping emergency gear stocked near disaster-prone areas means supplies can reach the field much faster. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T10#GNS315_U1_T10_h6)

question: In the popular SOAP charting format, what does the letter 'O' stand for?

options.A: Optimal outcome
options.B: Objective data
options.C: Ongoing order
options.D: Observed opinion

explanation: You've got this! 'O' is for objective data—the things you can actually measure and see, like vital signs and physical exam results. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T6#GNS113_U2_T6_h3)

question: When is a case-control study most useful to carry out?

options.A: When measuring the exact incidence rate of a condition
options.B: When investigating a rare disease
options.C: When studying a very rare exposure
options.D: When proving absolute cause and effect

explanation: Spot on! Since these studies start with people who already have the condition, they are brilliant for tracking down rare illnesses. [learn more](GST114_U2_T19#GST114_U2_T19_h6)

question: What is the most important rule when picking a theoretical framework for your study?

options.A: It must be a grand theory rather than a middle-range theory
options.B: It must be approved by the hospital nursing director
options.C: It must naturally match the specific research problem and variables
options.D: It must be the most recently published theory in nursing literature

explanation: Right! Your framework has to make logical sense with what you are trying to find out. Never force a mismatch. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T12#GNS217_U3_T12_h5)

question: Which quick physical check is critical before prescribing a combined estrogen-progestin oral contraceptive?

options.A: Chest X-ray imaging
options.B: Fasting blood glucose test
options.C: Blood pressure measurement
options.D: Routine eye examination

explanation: Always check the BP first! Estrogen can sometimes cause blood pressure to rise or increase clot risks, so checking baseline BP keeps your client safe. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T1#GNS225_U3_T1_h5)

question: What is the main goal of disease surveillance in community health?

options.A: To punish communities that fail to maintain basic sanitation
options.B: To eliminate all vector insects using chemical sprays
options.C: To detect and monitor disease patterns and potential reservoirs early
options.D: To manufacture and distribute expensive pharmaceutical drugs

explanation: Surveillance is like our radar system—it helps nurses spot disease trends and catch outbreaks before they blow up. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h5)

question: At what CD4+ cell count is an HIV infection typically classified as AIDS?

options.A: Below 500 cells per microliter
options.B: Below 1000 cells per microliter
options.C: Below 1500 cells per microliter
options.D: Below 200 cells per microliter

explanation: When the CD4 count drops below 200 cells per microliter, it shows severe immune weakness and meets the clinical definition of AIDS. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T13#GNS216_U6_T13_h1)

question: Why does having more sex hormone-binding globulin mean less active testosterone?

options.A: It binds to testosterone so tissues cannot use it
options.B: It blocks the pituitary gland from releasing luteinizing hormone
options.C: It speeds up the clearance of testosterone through the kidneys
options.D: It destroys the testosterone molecules completely

explanation: Think of sex hormone-binding globulin like a pair of handcuffs. Once it attaches to testosterone, the hormone is locked up and cannot do its usual job in the body. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T8#GNS121_U4_T8_h2)

question: Why might a struggling family find it hard to follow advice about eating a balanced diet?

options.A: Local health nurses refuse to give them recipe books
options.B: Daily survival and food costs take priority over long-term health
options.C: Traditional beliefs forbid the eating of vegetables
options.D: They lack basic interest in learning about nutrition

explanation: When money is tight, finding food for today always comes before thinking about long-term wellness. Empathy is key here! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T27#GNS225_U2_T27_h5)

question: What fields are combined in nursing informatics?

options.A: Pharmacology, anatomy, and clinical psychology
options.B: Public health, epidemiology, and health economics
options.C: Nursing science, computer science, and information science
options.D: Biology, chemistry, and hospital administration

explanation: Nursing informatics merges nursing principles with computer and information technology to improve data management and patient care outcomes. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T8#GNS113_U1_T8_h1)

question: What is the main goal of search and rescue operations when a disaster hits?

options.A: Clear debris and rebuild destroyed public infrastructure
options.B: Distribute food and clean water to affected communities
options.C: Locate, extricate, and deliver victims to medical care
options.D: Provide long-term rehabilitation for displaced families

explanation: You've got this! Search and rescue is simply about finding those who are missing, getting them out safely, and handing them over for medical treatment. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T3#GNS315_U5_T3_h1)

question: Why do we give nitroglycerin to a patient having chest pain from heart disease?

options.A: It dissolves existing blood clots inside the coronary arteries.
options.B: It slows down the electrical signals from the SA node.
options.C: It permanently removes fatty plaque from the artery walls.
options.D: It dilates blood vessels to improve blood flow and lower heart workload.

explanation: Spot on! Nitroglycerin relaxes the blood vessels, widening the coronary arteries and making it much easier for the heart to pump. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T10#GNS111_U2_T10_h6)

question: Why must you stay right by the patient during the first 15 minutes of a blood transfusion?

options.A: Hospital accreditation rules require physical presence to document vital signs
options.B: Most severe, life-threatening transfusion reactions occur during this initial window
options.C: Patients often feel lonely and anxious when receiving intravenous fluids
options.D: Pumps automatically lock out nurse access after fifteen minutes of running

explanation: Most bad reactions happen right at the beginning when the blood first hits circulation. Staying close lets you catch it instantly! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T13#GNS311_U2_T13_h6)

question: What makes a nutrient 'essential'?

options.A: It is only found in expensive dietary supplements.
options.B: The body cannot make it, so it must come from food.
options.C: The body produces it in massive quantities daily.
options.D: It provides zero calories but tastes sweet.

explanation: If our bodies can't manufacture it on their own, it's 'essential' that we eat it. Simple as that! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T001#GNS227_U1_T001_h4)

question: Why must disaster nurses actively watch out for compassion fatigue and practice self-care?

options.A: Patients will lose respect for nurses who show emotion
options.B: Nurses are immune to stress if they work fast enough
options.C: Hospital managers require daily wellness logs from every nurse
options.D: Prolonged exposure to trauma can lead to severe emotional burnout

explanation: So true! Seeing constant suffering wears down even the strongest nurses. Taking care of your own mental health keeps you and your patients safe. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T4#GNS315_U5_T4_h7)

question: Why can predictive formulas (like the Harris-Benedict equation) sometimes be misleading for critically ill patients?

options.A: They measure direct body heat rather than gas exchange
options.B: They require the patient to be placed inside a sealed heat chamber
options.C: They only provide estimates and may miscalculate actual needs during severe illness
options.D: They can only be used on healthy newborn infants

explanation: Formulas use averages for healthy people. But when a patient has severe burns or trauma, their body behaves unpredictably, so formulas can miss the mark. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T014#GNS227_U1_T014_h5)

question: What is the difference between intragroup and intergroup conflict?

options.A: Intragroup involves money, while intergroup involves medical errors.
options.B: Intragroup happens within the same team, while intergroup happens between different teams.
options.C: Intragroup is internal, while intergroup is external.
options.D: Intragroup only occurs at night, while intergroup occurs during the day.

explanation: Think of 'intra-' as *within* one group, and 'inter-' as *between* separate groups. Easy trick to remember! [learn more](GST321_U5_T3#GST321_U5_T3_h4)

question: What is the difference between a 'use-by' date and a 'best-before' date?

options.A: Use-by is for canned goods, while best-before is for fresh meat

question: A nurse notices a toddler has not started walking or babbling by the expected age. What is the most appropriate next step?

question: What is the main point of using data storytelling in healthcare?

question: What is a major safety challenge unique to home health nursing compared to working in a hospital ward?

options.C: Being barred from performing physical assessments on patients
options.D: Having no responsibility for coordinating multidisciplinary care

question: What does an autoclave primarily use to sterilize infectious medical waste?

options.A: High-pressure steam

question: Why is a multidisciplinary team necessary for managing long-term inherited degenerative disorders?

question: Why do red blood cells change into a sickle shape in this condition?

options.B: Haemoglobin S molecules stick together to form rigid rods when they release oxygen

question: A patient with active pulmonary tuberculosis is admitted to the ward. Which intervention is most crucial to interrupt the airborne transmission of this disease?

options.B: Placing the patient in a negative pressure isolation room
options.C: Washing all hospital floors with ordinary tap water daily
options.D: Encouraging family members to wear clean cloth gloves

question: How do nurses directly help make a hospital Drug Revolving Fund successful?

options.C: By importing foreign pharmaceuticals directly from overseas factories
options.D: By providing feedback on drug stock levels and ward consumption

explanation: As nurses, we work directly with patients and medications every day. Spotting low stock early and letting pharmacy know helps keep the supply chain smooth. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h6)

question: Why does a person exercising in a humid room find it hard to cool down?

options.A: Dermal blood vessels constrict automatically in humid air

options.C: The hypothalamus shuts down the body's internal thermostat
options.D: Sweat glands stop producing moisture when humidity increases

question: What is the main purpose of using MBO in a healthcare setting?

options.C: To connect daily staff duties with overall hospital goals
options.D: To increase the cost of running clinical wards

explanation: MBO bridges the gap between individual staff activities and the broader mission of the healthcare facility. [learn more](GST321_U2_T4#GST321_U2_T4_h1)

question: What is the main reason we dry a newborn baby off immediately after birth?

question: What three areas does the famous Donabedian model look at to measure healthcare quality?

options.A: Structure, process, and outcome

options.C: Admission, treatment, and discharge
options.D: Staffing, funding, and equipment

explanation: Remember the Donabedian trio: the setup (structure), what is actually done (process), and the final result for the patient (outcome). [learn more](GST319_U4_T2#GST319_U4_T2_h5)

question: What primary problem led to the invention of the Coronary Care Unit (CCU)?

options.A: High rates of severe bleeding during routine blood pressure checks

options.C: A massive shortage of beds for patients suffering from severe pneumonia
options.D: The frequent occurrence of surgical wound infections after heart operations

explanation: CCUs were created to continuously monitor heart patients so dangerous rhythms could be treated immediately before the heart stopped. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h4)

question: Which symptom in a newborn or young infant is a clear indication for urgent hospital referral?

options.A: Mild sneezing during the early morning hours

options.C: Inability to breastfeed or drink anything

question: Which type of female genital mutilation involves cutting and narrowing the vaginal opening?

question: A patient newly diagnosed with celiac disease is stressed about grocery shopping. What is your best first step as a nurse?

options.A: Advise the patient to avoid eating all packaged foods forever.

question: What do we call 'diagnostic overshadowing' when caring for a patient with a disability?

options.A: Overprescribing pain relief medication for chronic joint stiffness

options.D: Attributing all new symptoms mistakenly to the existing disability

explanation: It's a sneaky trap! This happens when we assume a new problem is just 'part of their usual condition' and forget to investigate properly. Always look closer! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T15#GNS225_U5_T15_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of values clarification exercises?

options.A: Helping individuals examine their personal beliefs and priorities

options.D: Diagnosing underlying psychiatric personality disorders

question: What is the main goal of patient safety in healthcare?

options.A: To eliminate the cost of hospital stays
options.B: To ensure doctors make all clinical choices
options.C: To speed up the hospital discharge process
options.D: To prevent accidental harm to patients

question: Which term covers both undernutrition and overnutrition?

options.A: Homeostasis
options.B: Anabolism
options.C: Metabolism

explanation: Malnutrition isn't just about not having enough food—it's an umbrella term for any poor nutrition, whether someone is eating too little or too much. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T001#GNS227_U1_T001_h8)

question: Which practice should nurses avoid when handling used injection needles?

options.A: Activating the safety device

options.D: Recapping the needle by hand

question: Why is collecting health data but never analyzing or using it considered a bad practice?

options.A: It automatically invalidates all future requests for international donor grants
options.B: It violates international copyright laws regarding health registers
options.C: It wastes valuable time and resources while failing to improve community health outcomes
options.D: It causes immediate supply chain shortages in urban pharmacies

explanation: Collecting data takes hard work from nurses and patients. If no one looks at it to make decisions, that effort goes to waste! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T21#GNS225_U2_T21_h6)

question: What is the main goal of social health insurance schemes?

options.A: To ensure that every citizen pays identical out-of-pocket fees
options.B: To prevent foreign nurses from practicing within the country
options.C: To pool financial risks so healthcare remains affordable for everyone
options.D: To eliminate the need for any government budget allocations

explanation: Health insurance pools everyone's contributions together so that if someone falls sick, the burden is shared rather than ruining them financially. [learn more](GST322_U3_T2#GST322_U3_T2_h7)

question: What happens to blood volume when sodium levels rise in the blood?

question: What exactly is water pollution?

options.A: The natural filtration of rainwater through soil layers

options.D: The normal movement of minerals from rocks into rivers

question: What is a major feature of employer-sponsored health insurance?

options.A: It forbids patients from seeing private medical doctors

options.D: It is provided by companies as part of worker compensation

question: Why is keeping a detailed maintenance log for cold chain equipment important?

question: What should a nurse do immediately after spotting a suspected Category 1 infectious disease?

question: Why is keeping a mum well-hydrated and nourished so vital during a long labour?

options.D: Maintaining adequate hydration and energy balance

question: A newborn has rigid, tightly locked overlapping skull bones after a very long, difficult labour. What do we call this?

options.D: Pathological moulding

question: Why do large arteries possess thick walls rich in elastic tissue?

question: What is the recommended angle for lifting the head of the bed for a patient on a mechanical ventilator?

question: What is the primary focus of Management by Objectives (MBO) in healthcare?

question: A patient with a history of excess cortisol production is most likely to show which physical sign?

question: How does progesterone help protect an early pregnancy?

question: What does the 'teach-back' method mean when teaching a patient?

question: A nurse uses a pain scale that somehow measures patient hunger instead of pain. Which quality is this tool lacking?

question: What part of the cardiovascular system do antiarrhythmic medications target?

question: What do we call the everyday living conditions, money, and environments that shape a person's health and life choices?

question: What is a common challenge in hospitals when national economic resources are limited?

question: Which of these is NOT a standard step in AMTSL?

question: Which of these is NOT a reliable source for finding new ways to improve care?

question: Who produces the majority of domestic food supply in Nigeria?

question: Which behavioral change do we most often see in young children after experiencing a traumatic emergency?

question: A patient arrives at the clinic with thick, sticky mucus blocking their airways and causing severe coughing. Which type of nebulized medication is most appropriate?

question: Which of these is NOT one of the traditional 'essential cleans' during delivery?

question: You are counseling a young woman who wants to eat healthier on a tight budget. What is your best approach?

question: As a nurse, if you perform FGM, which core ethical principle are you directly breaking?

question: A patient tells you they are a transgender man who is married to a man. What does this demonstrate?

question: What does the first delay in the Three Delays Model refer to?

question: Why are deep animal bites often left open instead of being stitched tightly right away?

question: What happens to a patient's metabolic rate during severe physiological stress like major trauma or sepsis?

question: Which of these is NOT a helpful community health strategy for managing sickle cell anaemia?

question: Your patient has severe vomiting, dry lips and mouth, and poor skin turgor. What should you suspect?

question: What does a genetic predisposition to a mental disorder mean?

question: When handling a wet plaster cast, why should nurses use the palms of their hands instead of their fingertips?

question: What is the main goal of health advocacy in community nursing?

question: When a disease is constantly present in a specific community or region, what is it called?

question: In the Health Belief Model, what do we mean by 'perceived susceptibility'?

options.D: Thinking a disease has no cure at all

question: What does a simple frequency distribution table show us?

question: How does showing respect for a family's household customs help your patient care?

options.C: It builds trust and encourages the family to cooperate with the care plan
options.D: It guarantees the patient will never experience complications

question: An elderly male patient after surgery is restless and feels a strong urge to pee, but nothing comes out. What should the nurse suspect first?

options.B: Renal tubular acidosis
options.C: Urinary retention
options.D: Transitional hyperplasia

question: What is the safest way for a new mother to clean her perineal area after using the toilet?

options.A: Soaking in soapy bathwater
options.B: Washing from back to front
options.C: Washing from front to back
options.D: Wiping vigorously with dry paper

question: A patient on warfarin for a heart condition starts taking a daily garlic supplement. What is the major concern here?

options.B: The warfarin will turn the garlic tablets into poison
options.C: The patient will develop severe vitamin C toxicity
options.D: The garlic will completely cure the heart condition overnight

question: What does an elevated reticulocyte count in a routine blood test usually indicate in a patient with sickle cell anaemia?

options.C: The spleen has successfully cleared all abnormal cells from circulation
options.D: The bone marrow is working hard to replace destroyed red blood cells

explanation: Reticulocytes are newly formed red blood cells. A high count shows the bone marrow is rushing to make new cells to make up for those lost to haemolysis. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h5)

question: Why do nurses treat the family as a single unit of care?

options.B: Families pay all medical bills together

options.D: It reduces hospital admissions in the district

question: In the SMART goal framework, what does the letter 'M' stand for?

question: A nurse wants to check if an elderly patient can safely cook and manage money at home. Which tool should she use?

options.D: Lawton IADL Scale

question: In patient safety, what is a 'near-miss'?

options.B: A patient complaint filed against a negligent nurse
options.C: A missed medication dose documented in the shift report
options.D: An error that reaches the patient and causes severe harm

explanation: Exactly! A near-miss is a close call—an error almost happened, but someone caught it just in time before it could affect the patient. [learn more](GST319_U6_T7#GST319_U6_T7_h2)

question: Why do we restrict fat in certain diets rather than cutting it out completely?

options.A: Completely removing fat causes immediate weight gain.

options.C: Fat-free foods are too expensive to produce.

question: Which of these is a critical warning sign that a patient with an ovarian cyst should report right away?

options.D: Feeling tired after a long day at work

question: Serum sickness is a classic example of which type of hypersensitivity reaction?

question: Why is it important to let the chest completely recoil (rise back up) between compressions?

question: What is the leading cause of unintentional injury death among adolescents worldwide?

question: Why must hospital menus in Nigeria include familiar local food staples?

question: What is the primary role of instructional materials in nursing education?

question: What is the medical name for the bluish color you see on a patient's skin when they lack oxygen?

options.D: Erythema

question: What is the first step in the risk management process?

question: What is a major nursing concern when an older adult has severe dental problems and missing teeth?

question: Which clinical sign suggests that a newborn with a skull injury may have underlying intracranial pressure?

options.D: An intense craving for frequent feeds

question: Which of these is a major risk factor for getting perineal tears when having your first baby?

options.D: Multiparity

question: What can happen if a licensed healthcare provider is caught in gross professional negligence?

options.C: The facility manager automatically assumes responsibility for the crime

question: A patient says he reaches climax much faster than he wants during intercourse. What is he experiencing?

question: What makes an event count as a natural disaster in healthcare?

options.D: An accident that occurs only within a hospital or clinic setting

question: When you face sudden stress, which two key hormones do your adrenal glands rush out?

options.D: Insulin and glucagon

question: What does the principle of equity mean in mental health promotion?

question: Which assessment technique uses a stethoscope to listen to sounds inside the body?

question: What is the best eating strategy for an HIV patient dealing with severe nausea?

question: Why must the objectives of an explanatory study be very specific?

question: Why might a patient with salpingitis feel deep pelvic pain during sexual intercourse?

question: How is the pia mater different from the dura mater?

question: The ultimate goal of inter-professional collaboration supported by assertiveness is...

question: A patient is having a full panic attack due to a phobia. What should be the nurse's very first priority?

question: What is the main reason nurses wash out (irrigate) a newborn's infected eyes with sterile saline?

question: What characterizes common cause variation in a healthcare process?

question: Which body measurement is most commonly used in the community to quickly screen young children for severe malnutrition?

question: What is azotemia in a patient with acute kidney injury?

question: Which way of giving out a survey lets a nurse directly clarify confusing items for the respondent?

question: As a nurse, what does providing holistic care to a patient with a physical disability really mean?

question: How do slow court cases affect the fight against illegal healthcare providers?

question: How do heavy seasonal rains often mess up food distribution in remote rural areas?

question: Which long-term skin condition of the vulva is strongly linked to a higher risk of cancer?

question: Which bedside tool is commonly used in emergencies to quickly check for internal belly bleeding?

question: How does low socioeconomic status typically impact a patient's long-term adaptation to a chronic illness?

question: What is the most crucial nursing check right after a neck biopsy or fine-needle aspiration?

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard nursing responsibility during a routine patient discharge?

question: Which health problem is most common among street populations due to a lack of clean drinking water and toilets?

question: During a severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis, what mainly causes the airway to block?

question: What is the main job of an Automated External Defibrillator (AED)?

question: What dietary advice is most appropriate for a nurse to give a patient managing Type 2 diabetes?

question: Where should your finished knot sit after tying a simple interrupted stitch?

question: Why shouldn't incident reporting be treated like a disciplinary tool?

question: What is a critical rule to follow regarding promises made to disaster survivors?

question: Which body publishes the famous Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM)?

question: At 32 weeks, a pregnant patient suddenly has high blood pressure and protein in her urine. What is the most likely cause?

options.B: Protecting patient privacy and maintaining strict confidentiality

options.D: Providing practical feedback on how easy a clinical software tool is to use

explanation: Correct! Software coding is left to the IT experts. Nurses focus on safe clinical use, patient privacy, and giving feedback on how well the tools work. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h6)

question: You want to ask ten exact admission questions across five different hospitals without changing a single word. Which format fits best?

options.A: Open-ended dialogue
options.B: Structured interview
options.C: Unstructured interview
options.D: Semi-structured interview

explanation: You nailed it! A structured interview is rigid on purpose—it keeps every single question identical so your data stays consistent across different sites. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T24#GNS224_U1_T24_h2)

question: Which life stage is especially known for triggering or worsening domestic violence?

options.A: Adolescence
options.B: Pregnancy
options.C: Retirement
options.D: Toddlerhood

explanation: Well done! Studies show pregnancy is a high-risk period where domestic violence often starts or suddenly gets worse. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T16#GNS324_U3_T16_h3)

question: A patient comes to the clinic with a sore on her labia that hasn't healed in four months. What should you suspect?

options.A: A normal hormonal change related to approaching menopause
options.B: A simple Bartholin gland cyst that will resolve on its own
options.C: A potential malignant vulval lesion requiring a biopsy
options.D: An acute yeast infection that needs oral antifungal medication

question: What patient detail is usually written on an ADR form to protect their privacy?

options.A: National ID number
options.B: Home address
options.C: Initials
options.D: Full residential phone number

explanation: Using just the patient's initials keeps their identity confidential while still letting the clinical team trace the record if needed. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T6#GNS215_U2_T6_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a common complication of Gallows traction?

options.A: Poor blood circulation
options.B: Trouble breathing
options.C: Skin breakdown
options.D: Permanent vision problems

explanation: Traction focuses on the legs, skin, and breathing, but it has zero connection to a child's eyesight. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T10#GNS221_U1_T10_h5)

question: Why are peer champions so valuable for sustaining long-term changes in a nursing unit?

options.A: They write all the hospital policies and clinical guidelines.
options.B: They handle the payroll and administrative duties for the ward.
options.C: They model the new behaviors and encourage their colleagues.
options.D: They are responsible for punishing staff who refuse to comply.

explanation: Peer champions lead by example on the floor, making it much easier for other nurses to adopt new ways with confidence. [learn more](GST319_U2_T5#GST319_U2_T5_h7)

question: Why is proper sampling important when conducting a descriptive survey in a hospital?

options.A: It guarantees that every single patient in the country will be cured
options.B: It removes the need to analyze numerical data at the end
options.C: It stops patients from answering survey questions incorrectly
options.D: It ensures the selected group accurately reflects the entire patient population

explanation: Good sampling means the few people you study are a true mini-version of the whole group, making your findings reliable. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h5)

question: Which bloodborne infections are most commonly spread through accidental needlestick injuries from poorly managed waste?

options.A: Rhinovirus and Influenza virus
options.B: Plasmodium falciparum and Trypanosoma
options.C: Rabies virus and Ebola virus
options.D: Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and HIV

question: What does a psychologically safe nursing classroom help students do?

options.A: Ignore hospital safety guidelines during patient care
options.B: Pass all nursing board examinations without studying
options.C: Skip difficult clinical shifts without facing any penalties
options.D: Admit what they do not know without fear of harsh judgment

question: How can you best support a newly diagnosed hearing-impaired patient who feels lonely and isolated?

options.A: Connecting the patient with local support groups and rehabilitation
options.B: Limiting family visits to reduce communication fatigue
options.C: Focusing solely on medical treatments without addressing feelings
options.D: Telling the patient to avoid all social gatherings permanently

explanation: Connecting them to support groups and rehab programs helps them realize they aren't alone and teaches them awesome new ways to communicate. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T14#GNS324_U4_T14_h7)
